title: Glossary
markdown:
The terms from the course, in alphabetical order. The lesson that introduces each one is in brackets.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **_Generic** | Chooses an expression by the type of another, at compile time. (7.03) |
| **_Static_assert** | A condition checked by the compiler; false stops the build. (7.03) |
| **Address** | The number of a byte in memory. `&x` gives the address of `x`. (3.01) |
| **AddressSanitizer** | A compiler option (`-fsanitize=address`) that checks every memory access and reports the first bad one. On the website: Memory checks. (4.06) |
| **Alignment** | Placing a value at an address that is a multiple of its size, which the processor reads fastest. (4.03) |
| **Amortised** | Averaged over many operations: a growing array's push is constant time on average even though it sometimes copies. (4.02) |
| **Anonymous member** | A struct or union inside another with no name, whose fields are reached directly. (7.03) |
| **argc / argv** | The number of command-line words and the array of them, passed to `main`. (3.05) |
| **Array** | A fixed number of values of one type, side by side in memory. (2.04) |
| **assert** | A check that stops the program with a message if a condition is false. (5.04) |
| **Atomic** | A variable whose operations happen as one indivisible step, from `<stdatomic.h>`. (7.05) |
| **Big-endian** | Storing the most significant byte of a number first. (5.02) |
| **Bit field** | A struct member with a width in bits: `unsigned flag : 1;`. (7.02) |
| **Bitwise operator** | `& \| ^ ~ << >>`: operators that work on each bit separately. (5.01) |
| **Bucket** | One slot of a hash table, holding the entries whose hash leads there. (6.05) |
| **Buffer overflow** | Writing past the end of an array into whatever memory follows. (2.04) |
| **C23** | The 2023 C standard: `bool` and `nullptr` keywords, `typeof`, `constexpr`, `#embed` and more. (7.03) |
| **Callback** | A function passed to another function to be called by it. (6.01) |
| **calloc** | Allocates heap memory set to zero. (4.01) |
| **Capacity** | How many elements a growing array has room for, as opposed to its length. (4.02) |
| **Cast** | Converting a value to another type explicitly: `(double)n`. (1.04) |
| **Collision** | Two keys landing in the same bucket of a hash table. (6.05) |
| **Comparison function** | A function returning negative, zero or positive, used by qsort and bsearch (8.02) |
| **Compiler** | The program that turns C source into machine code. (1.01) |
| **Compound literal** | An unnamed object written `(type){ ... }` where a value is needed. (7.03) |
| **Condition variable** | `cnd_t`: lets a thread sleep until another signals a change. (7.05) |
| **const** | Marks something read-only; `const T *p` cannot change what it points at. (3.04) |
| **Dangling pointer** | A pointer to memory that has been freed or to a local that no longer exists. (3.03) |
| **Declaration** | Tells the compiler a name and its type: a prototype or an `extern` variable. (2.02) |
| **Default argument promotions** | Extra arguments are widened: `char` and `short` to `int`, `float` to `double`. (7.01) |
| **Definition** | Creates the thing itself: a function's body or a variable's storage. Exactly one per program. (5.05) |
| **Dereference** | Following a pointer to the value it points at: `*p`. (3.01) |
| **Designated initializer** | An initializer that names its fields or positions: `{ .width = 10, [3] = 7 }`. (7.03) |
| **Double free** | Freeing the same heap block twice. (4.01) |
| **Element size** | The number of bytes of one element, passed with a void pointer so generic code can step through an array (8.02) |
| **enum** | A type whose values are named integer constants. (4.04) |
| **EOF** | The value input functions return at the end of the input. (2.01) |
| **errno** | A variable library functions set to an error code when they fail. (5.03) |
| **Exit code** | The number `main` returns: 0 for success. (1.01) |
| **extern** | Declares a variable defined in another file. (5.05) |
| **FILE** | The type of an open stream: a file, or `stdin`, `stdout`, `stderr`. (5.03) |
| **Fisher-Yates shuffle** | The fair way to shuffle: from the end, swap each element with a random one at or before it (8.06) |
| **Flexible array member** | A last struct member written `type name[];`, sized when the struct is allocated. (7.02) |
| **Function pointer** | A variable holding the address of a function, which can be called through it. (6.01) |
| **goto cleanup** | The idiom of jumping to shared cleanup labels at the end of a function on failure. (7.04) |
| **Hash function** | Turns a key into a number used to pick a bucket. (6.05) |
| **Hash table** | A structure that finds values by key in about constant time. (6.05) |
| **Header file** | A `.h` file of declarations that other files `#include`. (5.05) |
| **Heap** | Memory allocated with `malloc` that lasts until `free`. (4.01) |
| **Include guard** | `#ifndef` / `#define` / `#endif` around a header so it only counts once. (5.04) |
| **Inlining** | The optimiser pasting a function's body where it is called. (6.03) |
| **Integer promotion** | Small integer types such as char and short becoming int before arithmetic (8.05) |
| **Linked list** | A chain of nodes, each pointing to the next. (4.05) |
| **Linker** | Joins object files and libraries into a program, matching calls to definitions. (1.01, 5.05) |
| **Little-endian** | Storing the least significant byte first, as x86 and ARM do. (5.02) |
| **Load factor** | Entries divided by buckets in a hash table. (6.05) |
| **Macro** | A `#define` name the preprocessor replaces with text, possibly with parameters. (5.04) |
| **malloc / free** | Allocate and release heap memory. (4.01) |
| **Mask** | A number with 1 bits where you want to test, set or clear. (5.01) |
| **Memory leak** | Heap memory that is never freed. (4.01) |
| **mktime** | Turns a local struct tm into time_t and normalises out-of-range fields (8.03) |
| **Modulo bias** | The unfairness of rand() % n when the generator's range is not a multiple of n (8.06) |
| **Mutex** | `mtx_t`: lets one thread at a time into a critical section. (7.05) |
| **NULL** | The pointer that points at nothing. (3.01) |
| **Object file** | A `.o` file: one compiled source file, not yet linked. (5.05) |
| **Off-by-one** | A loop or index that goes one too far or stops one short. (2.01) |
| **offsetof** | A macro giving a field's distance in bytes from the start of its struct. (7.02) |
| **Optimiser** | The part of the compiler that makes code faster at `-O2`. (6.03) |
| **Ownership** | Which part of a program must free a block of memory; a function that returns new memory gives it to the caller (8.01) |
| **Padding** | Unused bytes the compiler puts in a struct to keep fields aligned. (4.03) |
| **Pointer** | A variable holding an address. (3.01) |
| **Pointer arithmetic** | Adding to a pointer moves it by whole elements: `p + 1` is the next one. (3.02) |
| **Preprocessor** | The first build stage, which handles lines starting with `#`. (5.04) |
| **Prototype** | A function's first line ending in a semicolon, declaring it. (2.02) |
| **qsort** | The standard library's sort, given a comparison function. (6.01) |
| **realloc** | Resizes a heap block, moving it if needed. (4.02) |
| **Recursion** | A function calling itself. (2.02) |
| **Return code** | A function's return value used to report success or the kind of failure. (7.04) |
| **Scope** | Where in the code a name can be used. (2.03) |
| **Seed** | The starting value of a random number generator; the same seed gives the same sequence (8.06) |
| **Segmentation fault** | The crash when a program touches memory it does not own. (3.01) |
| **Sentinel** | A special last argument, such as `NULL`, that marks the end of a variadic list. (7.01) |
| **setjmp and longjmp** | Save a point of execution and jump back to it from deeper calls, skipping everything between. (7.04) |
| **Shadowing** | A local hiding an outer variable of the same name. (2.03) |
| **Short-circuit** | `&&` and `\|\|` stopping as soon as the answer is known. (1.05) |
| **size_t** | The unsigned type for sizes and counts, printed with `%zu`. (2.04) |
| **sizeof** | Gives the size of a type or object in bytes. (1.02) |
| **Stack frame** | The memory a function call gets for its parameters and locals. (2.02) |
| **Standard error** | The output stream for messages and errors, kept apart from the results on standard output (8.04) |
| **static** | On a local: keeps its value between calls. On a global or function: private to its file. (2.03) |
| **stdint.h** | The header with exact-width types like `uint8_t` and `int64_t`. (5.02) |
| **strftime** | Formats a struct tm as text by a pattern such as %Y-%m-%d (8.03) |
| **String** | An array of `char` ending in `'\0'`. (2.05) |
| **String buffer** | A growable piece of text kept with its length and capacity, grown with realloc (8.01) |
| **struct** | A type grouping named fields. (4.03) |
| **struct tm** | A time broken into year, month, day, hour, minute and second; tm_year counts from 1900 and tm_mon from 0 (8.03) |
| **Tagged union** | A union with an enum saying which member is in use. (4.04) |
| **Terminator** | The zero byte `'\0'` that ends a string. (2.05) |
| **thrd_create** | Starts a C11 thread running a function `int f(void *)`. (7.05) |
| **ThreadSanitizer** | A compiler option (`-fsanitize=thread`) that reports data races while the program runs. (7.05) |
| **time_t** | A point in time as one number, usually seconds since 1970 UTC (8.03) |
| **typedef** | Gives a type another name. (4.04) |
| **Undefined behaviour** | Code the C standard sets no rules for, such as signed overflow; anything may happen. (6.02) |
| **union** | A type whose members share the same memory. (4.04) |
| **Use after free** | Using heap memory after it was freed. (4.01) |
| **Usual arithmetic conversions** | The rules that bring both operands to one type; with signed and unsigned of the same size, the signed one becomes unsigned (8.05) |
| **va_list** | The type that walks a variadic function's extra arguments with `va_start`, `va_arg` and `va_end`. (7.01) |
| **Valgrind** | A Linux tool that checks an unchanged program's memory use. (4.06) |
| **Variadic function** | A function whose parameter list ends in `...`, taking any number of extra arguments. (7.01) |
| **void \*** | A pointer to anything, which must be converted before use. (3.01) |
| **vsnprintf** | The va_list form of snprintf; with a size of 0 it measures how long the output would be (8.01) |
| **Warning** | A compiler message about legal but suspicious code. Treat them as errors. (1.01) |
